subject: Commit structure and minimum spend clarifications for hosted API
messages:
From: Aiden Lewis <aiden@streamline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Minimum monthly commit for hosted API?

Hi Marissa,

We're evaluating Redwood's hosted API for an in-app chat feature and trying to map the economics before presenting to finance. A few quick questions:

- Do you have a minimum monthly spend or commit for the hosted API today (we're not ready for Dedicated)?
- If commits are available, what are typical discount tiers vs PAYG and what are the minimum term lengths?
- Can commits be quarterly instead of monthly invoices? Procurement needs to know if they can start with a smaller/shorter commit.
- Any paperwork or PO requirements (Net 30/45)? Also curious if trial credits can be applied toward first month of a commit.

We expect initial volume around 1.5M tokens/month with spikey traffic during launches; curious how that maps to tiers.

Thanks,
Aiden
Aiden Lewis
Head of Product
Streamline AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aiden Lewis <aiden@streamline.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Minimum monthly commit for hosted API?

Hi Aiden — great questions, thanks for the context. Quick summary below; attaching the Q4 rate card and a sample term sheet for commits.

Short answers up front:
- No hard minimum to use the hosted API: PAYG is available immediately.
- We offer committed monthly spend tiers with meaningful discounts; commits start at $5,000/month for a 12-month term.
- We can discuss quarterly billing but discounts are typically tied to duration (12/24 months gives better rates).
- Trial credits can be applied toward the first invoice with an executed order form. PO/Net30 is common for commercial customers.

Tiered examples (illustrative pricing, see attached rate card for full details):
- PAYG: standard published per-token rates (no commit).
- 12-month commit: minimum $5k/month -> ~10% effective discount vs PAYG; $15k/month -> ~18% discount; $50k+/month -> bespoke pricing (25–35% typical range).
- 24-month commit: add ~5–8 pp improvement on discount vs 12-month.

Operational notes:
- Commits are flexible about how you consume the units; you get a committed spend credit each month and overages are billed at the PAYG rate (or we can include overage caps in the order form).
- No Dedicated required to get committed pricing — hosted can be used with a commit.

Next steps: if you can share a target monthly commit range (e.g., $5k / $15k / $50k), I can route a term sheet and finance can confirm billing/PO/net terms. Happy to set a 30-min call with Rishi to map expected concurrency and cost.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

Attachment(s): Redwood_rate_card_Q4_2025.pdf, Sample_commit_term_sheet.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aiden Lewis <aiden@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-08T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Minimum monthly commit for hosted API?

Hi Aiden — quick technical note from the SE side to help map the commit to expected spend.

Based on 1.5M tokens/month as a baseline:
- If you're using an LLM that's similar to our mid-tier generator profile, that equates to roughly $X per 100k tokens PAYG (see attached rate card for exact numbers).
- Example math: PAYG might be ~$0.80 per 1k tokens for model X (ballpark); at 1.5M tokens that's ~$1,200/month PAYG. A $5k/month commit would therefore be a safe starter that covers your base and burst buffer; a $15k/month commit reduces per-token cost significantly when you hit sustained usage and also gives you priority routing during bursts.

Operational considerations:
- Concurrency: hosted API supports continuous batching and prefix caching; if your traffic is very spiky we recommend enabling prefix caching and short-lived KV caching on hot prompts to reduce token usage.
- Overages: when a month exceeds committed spend, overage applies at PAYG rates unless you add an overage discount in the order form.

If you like, we can run a short eval with a 7–14 day load pattern to estimate per-token effective cost and latency — I can stand that up with temporary credentials.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Aiden Lewis <aiden@streamline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <procurement@streamline.ai>
Date: 2025-10-08T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Minimum monthly commit for hosted API?

Thanks Marissa/Rishi — helpful. A few clarifications from procurement:

- Can we do a 3-month trial commit (quarterly) at an intermediate discount (between PAYG and 12-month)? Procurement is pushing for shorter commitments initially.
- If we sign a 12-month at $15k/month, are there any onboarding credits we can apply to reduce the first-month cash outlay?
- Our legal/procurement will need an order form and PO; they prefer Net 30. Can you confirm Redwood accepts PO + Net 30 for this size?

Also CC'd Priya (procurement) — she may ping you for standard vendor terms.

Appreciate it,
Aiden

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aiden Lewis <aiden@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-09T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Minimum monthly commit for hosted API?

Hi Aiden — looping in quickly from finance/ops. We can accommodate your procurement asks. To accelerate things and make the first 90 days lower friction, Redwood is willing to offer the following promotional package if Streamline signs the order form by 2025-10-31: 

- Offer: 12-month commit at $15,000/month with an 18% effective discount vs PAYG pricing.
- Add two months of consumption credits (applied across the first six months) worth $15,000 total to offset initial spend.
- Net 30 via PO is acceptable for this deal size; we'll route standard vendor forms.

If you prefer a short-term trial commit, we can do a 3-month commit at $7,500/month with a smaller discount (approx 6–8%) and require prepayment or a PO with 50% upfront — procurement typically chooses one of those.

Marissa — please prepare the order form and include an overage cap option (we'll default to PAYG overage unless Streamline opts into a capped overage rate). Priya — I'll authorize signature on the order form once we confirm term.

Aiden — happy to hop on a quick call today or tomorrow to finalize, or Marissa can send the DocuSign link once the term is selected.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
